about: Wild chimpanzee datasets for ChimpBench, ranked by value for comparing real vs simulated ranging, movement trajectories, patrols and territory change (docs/datasets.md). Every entry was verified from its landing page or repository API on the date given; entries marked by 'helper' were verified by a scouting agent in the same session. Nothing here was downloaded except where status is 'downloaded'.

metricCodes.INC: excursion depth beyond the own boundary (incursions)

metricLevels.coarse: only at the dataset's coarse fix schedule
metricLevels.yes*: needs an extra layer the file lacks (boundary, neighbour range, labels)
metricLevels.unknown: not visible without opening the file

locationPolicy: Real coordinates stay in data/raw/ and never reach public/, docs/ or dist/. The guide shows only normalized maps: origin at the community UD centroid, distances in units of the equal-area radius R, arbitrary rotation, cells >= 0.1 R with fewer than 10 fixes or 3 days suppressed, no basemap, no dates finer than a month, anonymized individuals.

answers.openPatrolRoutesNote: No open dataset has labelled patrol tracks or mapped routes. Routes exist with the Ngogo, Gombe (ASU), Kanyawara (KCP) and Tai projects; raw unlabelled tracks exist on Movebank (Kanyawara 2017, Loango 2017-2019) behind owner permission.

spatial.crs: WGS84 decimal degrees, raw (analysis converts to UTM 36N, EPSG:32636)
spatial.fixSchedule: subsampled from 15-min focal-follow fixes to 1-2 fixes per individual-day, >= 3 h apart, 08:00-17:59, random (set.seed 42); individual-years with >= 30 points over >= 4 months

datasets.metricNotes: NET only between the 1-2 daily fixes (>= 3 h apart). INC: depth of West fixes inside Central's kernel and vice versa after 2018 (incursion-like excursions, not labelled patrols).

paperTargets.values: 134 min (15-348, SD 88); 2,456 m (SD 1,492); travel 58% of patrol time vs 14% on control days
paperTargets.derived: ~18 m/min overall; ~32 m/min (~0.53 m/s) while travelling (2,456 m / (0.58 x 134 min))

paperTargets.values: 58% entered neighbours' ranges, 42% along the boundary (p.1081); males per party 18.1 +/- 6.2 on patrol days vs 11.0 +/- 6.8; +17% odds per extra male (p.1082)
0.72/week; 13.0 +/- 5.6 members, 9.4 +/- 3.8 adult males; sector revisit intervals median 9-27 d (1-158) (pp.309-310); neighbours met or heard on 19/52 (Table 1)
median 88.5 min (3-595); median 8 males (1-13); 74.5 +/- 11.1% of males; annual median 4.5 (0-19); periphery visit = party >= 3 SD N or S of the yearly range centre

paperTargets.source: gilby2013 (Gilby, Wilson & Pusey 2013, Anim Behav 86:61-74; add to docs/research.md)
paperTargets.values: 7.3 patrols/year; each km the focal male travelled raised patrol odds by 1.63

patrol parties travel 2,500 +/- 2,300 m (South), 2,400 +/- 1,725 m (East); hill stops on 57.73% of moves toward the border vs 25.09% toward the centre; stops 38 +/- 65 min (hills), 30 +/- 32 min (low)

attack sites a median 2,105 m (1,370-2,850) outside the 80% range polygon and 495 m (410 m inside to 960 m outside) outside the 99% polygon (p.543); deep incursion = >= 1 km into the neighbour's range
median 1,867 m (288-4,406) from centre = 0.82 R; 85% acoustic only; 63% in the SE quadrant; 500 m grid
core 36% of area holds 85% of time; periphery 39.9% of area, 11% of time; periphery parties 5.9 vs 2.2 males
+6.4 km2 (+22.3%); 13 of 21 killings in the NE; NE used on 32.6% of days after June 2009
East 34 patrols / 39 encounters, South 6 / 27; home ranges East 32 km2, South 35 km2; border proximity as kernel %

sources.mitaniWatts2005 p.1081: two parts: (1) spatial - party moves to and along the boundary or into a neighbour's range; (2) behavioural - single file, close, silent, scanning stops, inspecting nests/wadges/faeces, rare feeding (paraphrase)
sources.wattsMitani2001 p.305: file formation, silent, not feeding, vigilant clusters that look and listen; vigilance until well back toward the centre (paraphrase)
sources.massaro2022: explicit note or cautious travel with looking/listening; spatial 'periphery visit' rule (>= 3 SD N or S of the yearly centre)
sources.lemoine2023: GPS rules: periphery = kernel value >= 75; stop = pause >= 5 min; direction toward border vs centre; advance/retreat in the 30 min after a stop
sources.wilson2004: deep incursion >= 1 km into the neighbour's range

patrolCriteria.noSpeedThreshold: No source gives a speed or straightness threshold; any such cut-off must be fitted on labelled patrol days, never on held-out targets.
gpsProxy: outbound leg from core to >= own 90-95% isopleth, then along or across it
party of >= 3 adult males (needs party membership or simultaneous fixes within ~50 m)
pauses >= 5 min near the edge (needs <= 1-min fixes)
entry beyond the own 95% isopleth into a neighbour's kernel (needs neighbour ranges)
extraFieldsNeeded: party membership per fix or simultaneous multi-individual fixes
patrol log dates (and ideally start/end times) for validation
